name: Agricola
metaTitle: Agricola Score Calculator (Full Farm Scoring Table)
metaDescription: Free Agricola score calculator for 1–4 players. Enter fields, pastures, crops and animals and it applies the scoring table, rooms, family and begging cards.
intro: Agricola's scoring table is the most confusing part of the game: every crop and animal has its own thresholds, and missing anything costs a point. Enter what each farm has and the calculator applies the table for you.

categories.label: Fields
categories.help: Plowed field tiles on your farm.

categories.label: Pastures
categories.help: Fenced pastures (each enclosed area counts once).

categories.label: Grain
categories.help: All grain you own, in your supply and planted in fields.

categories.label: Vegetables
categories.help: All vegetables you own, in your supply and planted in fields.

categories.label: Wild boar
categories.help: All wild boar on your farm.

categories.label: Unused farmyard spaces
categories.help: Spaces that are not plowed, fenced or built on. Each costs 1 point.

categories.label: Begging cards
categories.help: Begging cards taken when you could not feed your family.

categories.label: Card points
categories.help: Points printed on your improvements and occupations.

categories.label: Bonus points
categories.help: Extra points from card effects, such as the bonus from the Joinery or Pottery.

tiebreaker: If players are tied, they share the victory.

rules.heading: How scoring works in Agricola
body: After the final harvest at the end of round 14, every player scores their farm. Agricola rewards a balanced farm: for each type of field, crop and animal, having none costs you a point, and the points grow in steps as you have more.
Piling everything into one crop or animal rarely wins. The scoring table is built so that a little of everything beats a lot of one thing.

rules.heading: The scoring table
body: Fields: 0–1 scores −1, 2 scores 1, 3 scores 2, 4 scores 3 and 5 or more scores 4. Pastures: 0 scores −1, then 1, 2, 3 and 4 or more score 1 to 4.
Grain: 0 scores −1, 1–3 scores 1, 4–5 scores 2, 6–7 scores 3 and 8 or more scores 4. Vegetables: 0 scores −1, then 1, 2, 3 and 4 or more score 1 to 4.

Sheep: 0 scores −1, 1–3 scores 1, 4–5 scores 2, 6–7 scores 3 and 8 or more scores 4. Wild boar: 0 scores −1, 1–2 scores 1, 3–4 scores 2, 5–6 scores 3 and 7 or more scores 4. Cattle: 0 scores −1, 1 scores 1, 2–3 scores 2, 4–5 scores 3 and 6 or more scores 4.
Grain and vegetables count whether they are in your supply or still planted in fields.

rules.heading: Farmyard, house and family
body: Every unused space on your farmyard costs 1 point. Each fenced stable scores 1 point. Each clay room scores 1 point and each stone room scores 2; wooden rooms score nothing. Each family member, including newborns, is worth 3 points.
Each begging card, taken when you could not feed your family at harvest, costs 3 points.

rules.heading: Cards and bonus points
body: Major and minor improvements and some occupations show victory points. Some improvements, such as the craft buildings, also give bonus points for leftover resources at the end. Enter printed points and bonus points in their own rows.

faq.q: What happens if I have no sheep in Agricola?
faq.a: You lose 1 point. Each crop, animal, field and pasture type you have none of is worth −1.

faq.q: How many points is a family member worth?
Do planted grain and vegetables count?
faq.a: Yes. Count everything in your supply and everything still in your fields.
